canonical_question: Does the addition of 0.3 atom % Si improve oxidation resistance at all temperatures, or is the benefit limited to the 800–900 °C range as stated?

question_variants.question: Does the addition of 0.3 atom % Si improve oxidation resistance at all temperatures, or is the benefit limited to the 800–900 °C range as stated?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The addition of 0.3 atom% Si does not improve oxidation resistance at all temperatures. The benefit is limited to the 800–900 °C range, where the Si-containing HEA showed lower oxidation kinetics than the Al0.6CrFeCoNi HEA. However, at 1000 °C, the Si-containing HEA became inferior.

answers.answer: The oxidation resistance of the Si-containing HEA is temperature-dependent; it outperforms Al0.6CrFeCoNi at 800–900 °C but is inferior at 1000 °C.
answers.measurement_outcome: Lower oxidation kinetics at 800–900 °C; Inferior oxidation kinetics at 1000 °C compared to Al0.6CrFeCoNi
answers.mechanism: Not specified in the provided span, but the performance inversion is the key observation.
answers.boundary_limitation: Benefit is limited to lower temperatures (800–900 °C) and does not extend to 1000 °C.
evidence_spans: The ultrafine-grain microstructure is obtained using stationary friction processing performed at two different rotational speeds, 400 and 1800 rpm, for 5 min duration.

Processed samples demonstrate high depth of refinement (DOR) and ultrafine grain size (0.43–1 μm) at high rotational speeds along with significant phase transformations from BCC/B2 to FCC microstructure.
Oxidation kinetics of the ultrafine-grained sample is decelerated up to 12–48% in a temperature range of 850–1050 °C for a duration of 100 h.

source_evidence_spans: oxidation kinetics of the Si-containing HEA was lower than that of the Al 0.6 CrFeCoNi HEA at lower temperatures (800 and 900 °C) but became inferior compared to Al 0.6 CrFeCoNi at the higher temperature of 1000 °C.
